text: Medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTECs) establish T cell self-tolerance via autoimmune regulator (Aire) and peripheral tissue-specific self-antigens. RANK and CD40 signals regulate mTEC development: RANK signaling alone was essential during embryogenesis, while postnatal medullary microenvironment establishment required CD40–RANK cooperation. Ligation of RANK or CD40 on fetal thymic stroma induced mTEC development via TRAF6, NIK, and IKKβ. The first Aire+ mTECs emerged before αβ T cell repertoire selection, directed jointly by Rankl+ lymphoid tissue inducer cells and invariant Vγ5+ dendritic epidermal T cell (DETC) progenitors—the first thymocytes expressing gene rearrangement products. Aire+ mTECs then fostered Skint-1-dependent, Aire-independent DETC progenitor maturation, generating an invariant DETC repertoire. Thus developmental-stage-dependent RANK/CD40 cooperation and a Rank-mediated reciprocal DETC–mTEC link promote mTEC development, medullary microenvironment formation, and self-tolerance.
